title: Chhattisgarh Police Issue Show-Cause Notice to SP Over AK-47 Firing at Dussehra Ritual
excerpt: Rajnandgaon SP Ankita Sharma has been asked to explain the viral video of her firing an AK-47 after the Shastra Puja at Police Lines on October 20. Retired officers say weapon worship does not require firing; serving officers say blank rounds are part of the tradition.
body:
• The Chhattisgarh police headquarters on Thursday issued a show-cause notice to Rajnandgaon Superintendent of Police Ankita Sharma over the viral video of her firing an AK-47 during the Dussehra Shastra Puja.
  • The firing took place at Police Lines, Rajnandgaon, on October 20 after the traditional weapon-worship ceremony for Vijayadashami; Additional SP Kirtan Rathore was also filmed firing.
  • Similar firing videos surfaced from Raipur, Bilaspur, Raigarh, Durg, Kabirdham and Bastar districts.
  • The defence offered inside the force: blank rounds, called 'awazi kartoos,' are part of the Shastra Puja tradition and live ammunition is not used. The criticism, from retired Army and police officers: the manner of handling broke basic firearm-safety rules.

The Chhattisgarh police headquarters on Thursday issued a show-cause notice to Rajnandgaon Superintendent of Police Ankita Sharma after a video of her firing an AK-47 during a Dussehra weapon-worship ceremony was widely shared, with officers flagging possible violations of weapon-handling rules.

The firing took place at the Police Lines in Rajnandgaon on October 20 during the traditional Shastra Puja held for Vijayadashami, Rajnandgaon Range Inspector General Ajay Yadav said. In the video, Sharma, dressed in a saree, fires several rounds from the rifle after the ritual, in which police weapons and vehicles are worshipped. Additional SP Kirtan Rathore was also filmed firing. Yadav said headquarters had asked Sharma to explain her actions: "After receiving the SP's reply, I will record my observations and forward the matter to the police headquarters. Further action will be taken in accordance with the directions received from there."

A Tradition, or a Safety Breach?

Similar footage of police personnel firing weapons after the ritual surfaced from several other districts, including Raipur, Bilaspur, Raigarh, Durg, Kabirdham and Bastar. An IPS officer, speaking on condition of anonymity to PTI, said firing blank rounds — 'awazi kartoos' — is part of the Shastra Puja tradition observed across the state and that live ammunition is not used on such occasions, while cautioning that even a bullet fired into the air falls back and can injure people nearby.

https://x.com/htTweets/status/2113247427377705238

The criticism has come from veterans. Retired IPS officer R K Vij said ceremonial firing should happen only at a safe location with adequate precautions:

"The tradition is essentially about performing the worship of weapons, not firing them. Such firing carries the risk of accidents and should be avoided."

— R K Vij, retired IPS officer, to PTI

Former Army officer K J S Dhillon flagged what he described as basic handling violations in the video — a weapon pointed in different directions and people visible in the background — and Colonel Deepak Kumar, also retired, called the handling reckless and unprofessional. Deputy Chief Minister Arun Sao said the government would take cognisance of the matter, according to The Sun Today's report.

What Happens Next

Sharma, a 2018-batch IPS officer known for anti-Naxal operations in Chhattisgarh, must now reply to the notice. Headquarters said the comments accompanying the viral video had raised concerns about safety protocols and could affect the dignity of the police force. Because the same ritual firing was filmed in at least six other districts, any ruling on Sharma's reply will effectively set the rule for the whole state force: whether Shastra Puja firing with blanks is an accepted tradition, or a practice the headquarters intends to end.
